info.title: Coworkee.Cli
info.description: Coworkee command line: create a Coworkee application from switches or a JSON spec with modules, branding and entities, run it, add migrations, modules and entities, update the packages; MCP server for AI agents and launcher of Coworkee Studio.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
Create, run and maintain Coworkee applications.

Start with coworkee options (every switch of coworkee new) or coworkee spec example (an app as JSON for coworkee new --spec).
coworkee ui opens Coworkee Studio, a desktop wizard for the same. coworkee mcp is an MCP server for AI agents:
  claude mcp add coworkee -- coworkee mcp

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a Coworkee application; coworkee options describes every switch.

options.name: --output
options.description: Target folder (default: ./<name>, next to the spec with --spec).

options.name: --spec
options.description: Create the app from a JSON spec (coworkee spec example); switches given here win over the spec.

options.name: --template-spec
options.description: Start from a starter spec of the gallery (coworkee specs list); switches given here win over it.

options.name: --no-samples
options.description: Same as --samples false. [default: False]

options.name: --no-tests
options.description: Same as --tests false. [default: False]

options.name: --template-source
options.description: Install the template from this .nupkg or folder instead of nuget.org.

options.name: --user
options.description: A development user, seeded with a generated password (and into Keycloak with the same one): email[:role,role][:admin]; repeat for more users.

options.name: --title
options.description: Display title in the browser, the app bar, the sign-in pages and the Aspire dashboard (default: the name).

options.name: --samples
options.description: Catalog (products, brands, dashboard) and Documents modules with their pages, tests and demo data. (default: true)

options.name: --tests
options.description: API, migration, app host and page tests. (default: true)

options.name: --git
options.description: Run git init in the new folder. (default: false)

options.name: --airworks
options.description: A second client next to the Blazor app: the AirWorks web desktop (TypeScript) with windows, taskbar and apps for nearly everything the Blazor app offers: settings, files, data, chat, reports with their designer, the assistant and the administration. Same sign-in (and Keycloak), same api, theme and logo of the app; runs in the Aspire app host. (default: false)

options.name: --airworks-packages
options.description: Where the AirWorks client takes @coworkee/client and @coworkee/airworks from: the tarballs inside the template (no npm registry needed for them) or npm in the version of the template. (default: bundled) Only used with airworks.

options.name: --pwa
options.description: Web manifest, service worker and offline page: the app installs on phones and desktops and opens without the browser bar. With notifications users switch on Web Push per device. (default: true)

options.name: --repository
options.description: GitHub repository of the app as owner/repo, e.g. acme/shop: the README gets a QuickRun badge that starts the app from there with one click.

options.name: --auditing
options.description: Pages for the audit trail, entity history and restore. The trail itself is always written. (default: true)

options.name: --notifications
options.description: In-app notifications with mail digests. (default: true)

options.name: --chat
options.description: Direct and group chat with realtime delivery. (default: true)

options.name: --reports
options.description: Dashboards over the OData entity sets with charts, KPIs, tables and filters, aggregated on the server. (default: true)

options.name: --ai
options.description: Assistant page, MCP endpoint and tool call audit; every permitted command becomes a tool (provider and key in the settings). (default: true)

options.name: --backup
options.description: Backups and restore of the database from the admin pages. (default: true) Only used with database = postgres.

options.name: --files
options.description: Folders and files of the organisation with preview, upload and per-folder permissions. (default: false)

options.name: --features
options.description: Features switched per tenant, editions and the tenant administration of the host. (default: false)

options.name: --social
options.description: Comments, tags and star ratings for any entity, opted in per entity type. (default: false)

options.name: --workflows
options.description: States and transitions per entity type, approvals by roles or users with deadlines, reminders and escalation, a history, the approvals inbox; declared in code. With the samples, products go through an approval. (default: false)

options.name: --elsa
options.description: Elsa Workflows 3 in the api: its tables in the app's database, its api under /api/elsa for the permission Workflows.Elsa.Manage, activities and triggers for Coworkee workflows. Elsa Studio runs as its own app. (default: false) Only used with workflows.

options.name: --elsa-studio
options.description: Elsa Studio, the visual designer, as an app of its own in the app host: signs in at the auth server like the web app, lets in users with the permission Workflows.Elsa.Manage and works with the Elsa API of the api. The app's navigation links to it. (default: false) Only used with elsa.

options.name: --webhooks
options.description: Outgoing webhooks: admins register endpoints that get signed events about entity changes, workflow transitions and the app's own events, with retries and a delivery log. With the samples, products send events. (default: false)

options.name: --extended-attributes
options.description: Free key/value attributes for any entity without schema changes (the Documents sample brings it anyway). (default: false)

options.name: --elasticsearch
options.description: Elasticsearch index; the app host adds an Elasticsearch container. (default: false)

options.name: --event-bus
options.description: Integration events through the transactional outbox. (default: none)

options.name: --client-entities
options.description: The browser keeps copies of OData sets marked [ClientEntity] and filters them locally. Entities of the spec with clientEntity switch it on. (default: false)

options.name: --keycloak
options.description: Keycloak container as external sign-in, with a realm for the app. (default: false)

options.name: --storage
options.description: Where uploaded files and backups go. (default: fileSystem)

options.name: --ai-provider
options.description: Model provider of the assistant (with the AI assistant); changeable later on the AI page of the app. (default: anthropic) Only used with ai.

options.name: --ai-model
options.description: Model of the AI provider (Azure OpenAI: the deployment name); empty takes the provider's default. The key never goes into the spec: user secrets of the app host, Parameters:ai-apikey. Only used with ai.

options.name: --ai-endpoint
options.description: Base address of the AI provider, for Azure OpenAI, openAICompatible or a provider behind a proxy; empty takes the provider's address. Only used with ai.

options.name: --redis
options.description: Redis container in the app host: SignalR backplane, shared presence, cache invalidation and sign-in sessions across instances. (default: true)

options.name: --grafana
options.description: Grafana with Prometheus, Loki, Tempo and an OpenTelemetry collector in the app host: metrics, logs and traces of every service, the app database and ready dashboards. Sign-in with the app's administrator, and Keycloak when it is on. (default: true)

options.name: --web-data-studio
options.description: WebDataStudio, a database studio in the browser, connected to the app database. Sign-in with the app's administrator, and Keycloak when it is on. (default: true)

options.name: --aspire-ui
options.description: AspireUI, a web UI to host and try more apps and stacks next to the app, in the app host. Its apps show up on the admin page Services. Sign-in with the app's administrator, and Keycloak when it is on. (default: false)

options.name: --database
options.description: Database engine of the app; the app host starts it and the initial migration is made for it. (default: postgres)

options.name: --theme
options.description: Default theme of the installation. (default: Ocean)

options.name: --primary-color
options.description: Primary brand color #rrggbb. With a brand color the app gets its own theme (named like the title), based on the chosen theme, as default.

options.name: --secondary-color
options.description: Secondary brand color #rrggbb.

options.name: --logo
options.description: Logo file (svg, png, ...); the CLI copies it into the web client. It shows in the app bar, the browser tab and on the sign-in pages. (default: coworkee-icon.svg)

options.name: --sign-in-layout
options.description: Layout of the sign-in pages. (default: Slide)

options.name: --sign-in-media
options.description: Image or video next to the sign-in form: a local file (copied into the web client) or an http(s) address. Only used with signInLayout = Split or Slide, or loadingScreen = SignInMedia.

options.name: --sign-in-media-side
options.description: Side of the sign-in media. (default: Left) Only used with signInMedia.

options.name: --loading-screen
options.description: Background of the app's loading screen while the WebAssembly app loads. (default: Animated)

options.name: --mapping
options.description: Default mapping of generated entities to their DTOs; an entity can choose its own. (default: manual)

options.name: --languages
options.description: Languages the app offers from the start. 23 languages ship with the library; the others are machine translated at the first start with the translation service. Administrators switch more on later on the Languages page. Empty offers English and German.

options.name: --default-language
options.description: Language of users who chose none and whose browser asks for none of the offered ones. (default: en)

options.name: --translation-provider
options.description: Translates the texts a language lacks: at the first start, when a language is switched on, or on request. Changeable later in the settings (Translation). (default: libreTranslate)

options.name: --translation-source
options.description: The language translations start from. Texts are written in English; German starts from the shipped German wording where there is one. (default: en)

options.name: --color-mode
options.description: Light, dark or the system's mode as default of the installation; every user can switch it in the app bar. (default: system)

options.name: --registration
options.description: Visitors can register on the sign-in page (setting Account.AllowRegistration, changeable later). (default: true)

options.name: --github-actions
options.description: A workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) that builds the solution and runs its tests on every push and pull request. (default: false)

options.name: --devcontainer
options.description: A .devcontainer with the .NET SDK and Docker in Docker for GitHub Codespaces and VS Code. (default: false)

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Name of the app, used for projects and namespaces (default: the name in the spec).

commands.name: options
commands.description: List every switch of coworkee new and the spec, with default, choices and when to use it.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the catalog as JSON: id, flag, group, title, description, kind, default, choices, pros, cons, when to use. [default: False]

commands.name: spec
commands.description: App specs for coworkee new --spec: JSON with name, options, branding and modules with entities.

commands.name: schema
commands.description: Print the JSON Schema of a spec.

commands.name: example
commands.description: Print an example spec.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Check a spec; prints the problems and exits with 1 when there are any.

commands.name: current
commands.description: Print the spec of the app in this folder: .coworkee/app.json, or for older apps the options its files show.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Print what a spec creates: the library modules on and off, every other option with its value and your own modules. A spec lists only what differs from the defaults.

commands.name: specs
commands.description: Starter specs that come with the CLI: a CRM, a helpdesk, a shop and more. coworkee new MyApp --template-spec <id> creates one.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the starter specs with id, tags and what they contain.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Print a starter spec as JSON, e.g. to save it and change it: coworkee specs show crm > crm.json

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: Id of the starter spec, see coworkee specs list.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run the Aspire app host of the solution in the current folder.

commands.name: migrations
commands.description: Manage database migrations.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add an EF Core migration to the infrastructure project.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Name of the migration, for example AddOrders.

commands.name: db
commands.description: The app's local development database: reset, seed, backup and restore.

commands.name: reset
commands.description: Delete the database: the app host's data volume or the SQLite file. The next start migrates and seeds it again.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask before deleting or overwriting data. [default: False]

options.name: --volume
options.description: The data volume, when the app has several (run from several folders).

commands.name: seed
commands.description: Migrate the database and seed the demo users and roles (runs the migrations project against the running database).

options.name: --volume
options.description: The data volume, when the app has several (run from several folders).

commands.name: backup
commands.description: Back the database up: pg_dump or BACKUP DATABASE in the running container, or a copy of the SQLite file.

options.name: --volume
options.description: The data volume, when the app has several (run from several folders).

commands.name: restore
commands.description: Restore a backup of coworkee db backup; stop the app first for SQLite and SQL Server.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Do not ask before deleting or overwriting data. [default: False]

options.name: --volume
options.description: The data volume, when the app has several (run from several folders).

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A backup of coworkee db backup.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Turn on options of an existing app (modules, infrastructure, languages, ...): the template's changes are merged into your files, conflicts go to .rej files, then a migration is added.

options.name: --spec
options.description: Bring the app to this spec: its options, and its modules and entities the app does not have yet.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the plan and change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --template-source
options.description: The Coworkee.Templates .nupkg or folder of the app's version (default: the app's local feed, then nuget.org).

options.name: --no-migration
options.description: Do not add a migration afterwards. [default: False]

arguments.name: OPTIONS
arguments.description: Option ids, each optionally followed by its value: reports, eventBus rabbitMq, languages fr,it, ai openAI (coworkee options lists them).

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Turn options of an existing app off; only when every file it touches is still as the template wrote it or merges cleanly.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the plan and change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --template-source
options.description: The Coworkee.Templates .nupkg or folder of the app's version (default: the app's local feed, then nuget.org).

options.name: --no-migration
options.description: Do not add a migration afterwards. [default: False]

arguments.name: OPTIONS
arguments.description: Option ids, each optionally followed by its value: reports, eventBus rabbitMq, languages fr,it, ai openAI (coworkee options lists them).

commands.name: module
commands.description: Manage feature modules.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add a feature module with an entity: table, permissions, OData set, endpoints, validation and a Blazor page.

options.name: --entity
options.description: Name of its first entity (default: the module name without a trailing s).

options.name: --property
options.description: A property as Name[:type][:required][:maxLength][:flag][:key=value], e.g. Number:string:required:50:unique, Total:money, Status:enum=OrderStatus:default=Open:facet, Customer:ref=Customer:required or Customer:ref=Crm.Customer:onDelete=cascade. Flags: required, unique, display, facet, searchable. Keys: enum, ref (reference), referenceDisplay, onDelete (restrict, cascade, setNull), inverse, default, label, precision, scale, searchable. Types: string, int, long, decimal, double, bool, dateTime, guid, dateOnly, timeOnly, text, email, url, money, enum, reference. Repeat for more (default: Name:string:required:200).

options.name: --enum
options.description: An enum for enum properties as Name=Value1,Value2, e.g. OrderStatus=Open,Paid,Shipped; written to the contracts. Repeat for more.

options.name: --plural
options.description: Plural of the entity for table, OData set, route and page (default: name + s).

options.name: --client-entity
options.description: Mirror the OData set in the browser (adds Coworkee.Client.Blazor.ClientEntities when missing). [default: False]

options.name: --mapping
options.description: DTO mapping: Manual (a ToDto method) or Mapperly. [default: Manual]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Name of the module, for example Orders.

commands.name: entity
commands.description: Manage entities of feature modules.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add an entity to a generated module: table, permissions, OData set, endpoints, validation and a Blazor page.

options.name: --property
options.description: A property as Name[:type][:required][:maxLength][:flag][:key=value], e.g. Number:string:required:50:unique, Total:money, Status:enum=OrderStatus:default=Open:facet, Customer:ref=Customer:required or Customer:ref=Crm.Customer:onDelete=cascade. Flags: required, unique, display, facet, searchable. Keys: enum, ref (reference), referenceDisplay, onDelete (restrict, cascade, setNull), inverse, default, label, precision, scale, searchable. Types: string, int, long, decimal, double, bool, dateTime, guid, dateOnly, timeOnly, text, email, url, money, enum, reference. Repeat for more (default: Name:string:required:200).

options.name: --enum
options.description: An enum for enum properties as Name=Value1,Value2, e.g. OrderStatus=Open,Paid,Shipped; written to the contracts. Repeat for more.

options.name: --plural
options.description: Plural of the entity for table, OData set, route and page (default: name + s).

options.name: --client-entity
options.description: Mirror the OData set in the browser (adds Coworkee.Client.Blazor.ClientEntities when missing). [default: False]

options.name: --mapping
options.description: DTO mapping: Manual (a ToDto method) or Mapperly. [default: Manual]

arguments.name: MODULE
arguments.description: The module that gets the entity, created with coworkee module add.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: Name of the entity in singular, for example Invoice.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Import entities from a database, an OpenAPI document or a CSV file into a module of the app, or into a spec.

options.name: --from
options.description: What to read: db (Postgres, SQL Server or SQLite), openapi (OpenAPI 3 JSON) or csv.

options.name: --module
options.description: Module of the entities (default: the database name, the API title or the CSV file name).

options.name: --tables
options.description: Only these tables or schemas, comma separated, e.g. orders,customers.

options.name: --provider
options.description: db: postgres, sqlServer or sqlite (default: guessed from the connection string).

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the spec and the problems, change nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --spec-out
options.description: Write the module into this spec file (added to an existing spec) instead of the app.

arguments.name: SOURCE
arguments.description: db: a connection string or SQLite file; openapi: a JSON file or http(s) address; csv: a file with a header row.

commands.name: texts
commands.description: Work with the texts of the library.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Copy the library texts of a language into the app's translation file so you can change them. Existing keys keep their text, new keys are added at the end.

options.name: --lang
options.description: Language code of the library texts, for example fr (en exports the keys as texts).

options.name: --keys
options.description: Only the keys that match: a glob with * and ?, or a regular expression between slashes, for example "Filter*" or "/^Sign/".

options.name: --out
options.description: Target file (default: src/<App>.Contracts/Localization/<lang>.json of the solution here).

commands.name: update
commands.description: Set the Coworkee package version of the solution, apply the upgrade rules of the versions in between and list the manual steps.

options.name: --version
options.description: Coworkee version to use (default: the newest on nuget.org).

options.name: --prerelease
options.description: Allow prerelease versions when looking up the newest. [default: False]

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Show the breaking changes and what would change, change nothing. [default: False]

commands.name: self-update
commands.description: Update the coworkee CLI and Coworkee Studio (when installed) to the newest version. For the Coworkee packages of an app see coworkee update.

options.name: --version
options.description: Version to install (default: the newest on nuget.org).

options.name: --prerelease
options.description: Allow prerelease versions when looking up the newest (always on when this CLI is a prerelease). [default: False]

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Write the deployment artifacts of the app and its tools: Docker Compose, Azure Container Apps (Bicep) or Kubernetes (Helm).

options.name: --output
options.description: Folder for the artifacts, default deploy/<target> in the solution.

options.name: --no-build
options.description: Do not build the container images (compose). [default: False]

options.name: --without
options.description: Leave a tool of the app host out of the deployment, e.g. --without grafana.

options.name: --with
options.description: Deploy a tool that stays out by default: --with mailpit for a test deployment without a real mail server.

options.name: --admin-email
options.description: Email of the first administrator (compose; asked for, or admin@<app>.local).

arguments.name: TARGET
arguments.description: compose (Docker Compose on one host), azure (Azure Container Apps) or k8s (Kubernetes). [default: compose]

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check the tools a Coworkee application needs and whether their versions match the app.

commands.name: ui
commands.description: Open Coworkee Studio, the desktop wizard that configures and creates an app with this CLI. Installs or updates the global tool Coworkee.Studio to the CLI version first; other arguments (for example --spec app.json) go to coworkee-ui.

options.name: --studio-version
options.description: Studio version to install (default: the version of this CLI).

options.name: --prerelease
options.description: Install the newest prerelease of Coworkee Studio instead of the CLI's version; ignored with --studio-version. [default: False]

options.name: --add-source
options.description: Additional NuGet source for the Studio package, e.g. a folder with local packs.

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Run an MCP server over stdio, so AI agents can create and extend Coworkee apps (coworkee mcp --help shows how to register it).
